components.description: Motivation: LLM opacity, its real-world stakes, and the limits of existing explainability approaches.

nodes.name: LLM inference is opaque
nodes.description: LLMs exhibit broad capabilities, yet their inference remains opaque: decision factors are unobservable and generated explanations often lack faithfulness.

nodes.name: Opacity hinders high-stakes adoption
nodes.description: This opacity hinders adoption in high-stakes domains, risking confident hallucinations and biases in medicine and fictitious legal precedents that undermine accountability.

nodes.name: Attribution/attention methods are correlational
nodes.description: Attribution and attention-based explainability methods are primarily correlational, whereas faithful explanations require causal evidence.

nodes.name: Counterfactual causal-graph methods remain local/input-centered
nodes.description: Counterfactual methods using causal graphs over textual variables provide stronger causal evidence but typically remain local and input-centered: they quantify a given factor's causal effect but do not recover the model's high-level inference.

nodes.name: Mechanistic interpretability is low-level and often misaligned with stakeholder needs
nodes.description: Mechanistic interpretability targets internal components like neurons and circuits, providing a valuable low-level science but is often misaligned with the explanations stakeholders actually need.

nodes.name: Missing: global causal account of concept organization
nodes.description: What remains missing is an applicable explainability method providing a global, causal account of how a model organizes human-interpretable concepts and reduces them to a prediction.

components.description: Core reframing: using causal graphs to model LLM inference itself rather than the external world.

nodes.name: Prior causal-graph work models external-world processes
nodes.description: Prior work uses causal graphs, and sometimes LLMs, to recover causal graphs of external-world processes (concepts → text → prediction, graph usually assumed a priori).

nodes.name: This paper models LLM inference itself
nodes.description: Instead, this paper uses causal graphs to model LLM inference itself (text → concepts → prediction), providing a transparent view of how the model perceives and organizes high-level concepts to produce a prediction.

nodes.name: The graph is itself the explanation; nothing assumed a priori
nodes.description: In this new setting, the graph is itself the explanation, and both the relevant concepts and their causal relations must be inferred rather than assumed in advance.

components.description: Positioning relative to the three senses of causal graphs in LLM interpretability, and relative to the closest related work (COAT).

nodes.name: Sense 1: mechanistic-interpretability graphs over model internals
nodes.description: In mechanistic interpretability, causal graphs are defined over model-internal components (attention heads, neurons, residual-stream directions), abstracting away the complete computation to retain only components hypothesized to mediate a targeted behavior.

nodes.name: Sense 2: graphs enabling causal-effect estimation of concepts on predictions
nodes.description: Causal graphs are also used to enable estimation of causal effects of high-level concepts on predictions (via counterfactuals, matching, adjustment), where the graph is usually assumed in advance and describes concepts → text → prediction.

nodes.name: Sense 3 (this paper): graphs describing the model's high-level reasoning
nodes.description: The paper introduces a third utility: causal graphs describing the model's high-level reasoning (text → concepts → prediction), where the graph is the explanation and has received no prior attention in the literature.

nodes.name: COAT is the closest related work but targets real-world structure
nodes.description: COAT (Liu et al. 2024) also uses an LLM to propose concepts and applies causal discovery, but aims to recover real-world causal structures and focuses on local Markov blankets for causal effect estimation.

nodes.name: Departure 1: recover the full graph, not a local Markov blanket
nodes.description: Because the goal is to characterize the model's internal reasoning rather than estimate a real-world effect, this work recovers the full graph from text to prediction rather than only a local Markov blanket, to capture the complete reasoning process.

nodes.name: Departure 2: MCMC-inspired counterfactual augmentation for sparse coverage
nodes.description: Because observational data sparsely cover the model's internal decision space, this work introduces an MCMC-inspired counterfactual augmentation procedure to actively expand the concept space for more robust graph discovery.

components.description: The data-coverage bottleneck in causal discovery and why the LLM setting makes it tractable.

nodes.name: Reliable structure learning needs representative coverage
nodes.description: A central challenge in causal discovery is data coverage: reliable structure learning requires a representative sample spanning diverse combinations of concept values.

nodes.name: Achieving coverage often requires costly/impractical/unethical interventions
nodes.description: In many domains, obtaining such coverage requires costly, impractical, or unethical interventions.

nodes.name: LLM mechanism makes counterfactual generation cheap
nodes.description: Because the mechanism under study is an LLM, the model itself can be prompted to generate counterfactual texts in which a targeted concept is altered while the remaining context stays stable, making the coverage bottleneck more tractable.

nodes.name: MCMC-inspired algorithm iteratively expands and filters
nodes.description: The MCMC-inspired algorithm iteratively proposes counterfactual chains and rejects unfaithful candidates, producing a denser, higher-quality concept space for robust causal discovery.

components.description: Formal setup: concept vectors, the LLM-inference causal graph, and its structural constraints.

nodes.name: Causal Graph framework adopted, relaxed to allow cycles
nodes.description: The method adopts Pearl's Causal Graph framework, relaxed to admit cyclic dependencies, acknowledging potential reciprocal influences among concepts an LLM uses internally.

nodes.name: Concept-extraction function maps text to a concept vector
nodes.description: A concept-extraction function ϕ maps input text x to a concept vector [l_c1,...,l_cn], where each l_ci is a categorical variable over subsets S ⊆ Y indicating which classes the LLM perceives concept ci to support (∅ = absent, Y = non-discriminative).

nodes.name: Graph defined over text, concepts, and prediction
nodes.description: The LLM's inference process is represented as a directed graph G=(V,E) with V = {X} ∪ C ∪ {Ŷ}, capturing high-level causal flow from input text through LLM-perceived concepts to the prediction.

nodes.name: Structural constraints: X is root, Ŷ is sink
nodes.description: Three structural constraints are imposed: X has only outgoing edges (root), Ŷ has only incoming edges (sink), and the text's effect on prediction is mediated by the concept variables.

nodes.name: Task reduces to recovering C and E
nodes.description: Given these constraints, the task reduces to recovering the concept set C and edge set E.

components.description: Phase 1-2 of the pipeline: label prediction and discriminative concept discovery/filtering.

nodes.name: Label Prediction substitutes LLM predictions for ground truth
nodes.description: Ground-truth labels in D are replaced with the LLM's own predictions ŷ=f(x); all downstream phases use these predicted labels so the recovered graph reflects the model's perspective rather than dataset labels.

nodes.name: Concepts proposed iteratively over class-balanced batches
nodes.description: Discriminative Concept Discovery processes training data in small, class-balanced batches; for each batch, the model proposes new candidate concepts which are added to the accumulating concept set C.

nodes.name: Concepts periodically filtered by relevance and discriminativeness
nodes.description: Every ten batches, accumulated concepts are annotated and filtered, retaining only concepts whose assigned value maps to a strictly partial subset of classes (neither ∅ nor Y) in a fraction of examples exceeding threshold τ=1/|Y|.

nodes.name: Filtering removes non-expressed and non-discriminative concepts
nodes.description: This filtering removes concepts that are rarely expressed in text (providing little evidence for a text-to-concept edge) and concepts broadly aligned with all classes (providing little evidence for a concept-to-prediction edge).

nodes.name: Final concept set fixed after test-set filtering pass
nodes.description: After processing all training batches, test examples are annotated with concept vectors and the same filtering criterion is applied once more, yielding the final concept set C.

components.description: Phase 3 of the pipeline: MCMC-inspired counterfactual data expansion, including the Metropolis-Hastings-like acceptance test.

nodes.name: Expansion operates in text space, not directly in concept space
nodes.description: Rather than operating directly in the discrete concept space, the algorithm operates in raw text space: the LLM proposes a textual perturbation, which is mapped to a concept vector by ϕ and retained only if it induces the intended conceptual shift.

nodes.name: Operating in text space preserves linguistic coherence
nodes.description: Operating in text space preserves linguistic coherence while allowing exploration of realizable regions of the concept space, i.e., configurations expressible by natural text.

nodes.name: Each example initiates an independent expansion chain
nodes.description: Each original training example initiates an independent expansion process lasting K=11 steps, iterating through concepts and sampling a target class y* to determine a directional shift (MORE/LESS).

nodes.name: Acceptance test requires target alignment and minimal side effects
nodes.description: A proposal is accepted (akin to a Metropolis-Hastings test) if it achieves the intended target alignment for the targeted concept and the count of drifted non-target concepts is bounded by a small tolerance ϵ.

nodes.name: Recursive refinement re-prompts on failure
nodes.description: If a proposal fails either acceptance condition, the LLM is re-prompted with feedback on which criterion was violated, up to R=5 regeneration attempts per concept; if all fail, no sample is appended for that concept.

nodes.name: Expansion densifies the concept manifold for causal discovery
nodes.description: The MCMC-inspired expansion densifies the latent concept space by exploring combinations beyond the original dataset, stochastically exploring the valid concept manifold and providing richer support for causal discovery.

components.description: Phase 4 of the pipeline: causal discovery via σ-CG, and why σ-CG was chosen.

nodes.name: σ-CG chosen for cyclic, discrete-variable compatibility
nodes.description: σ-CG (Forré and Mooij 2018) is chosen because it accommodates cyclic causal structures, which may arise in LLM inference and cannot be ruled out a priori, and it supports the discrete variables produced by the concept annotations.

nodes.name: σ-CG applied to the expanded dataset
nodes.description: σ-CG is applied to the expanded, annotated dataset D_mcmc, obtaining a directed graph G over the variables V.

nodes.name: Ŷ enforced as the unique sink during orientation
nodes.description: As background knowledge, the algorithm imposes that ŷ is the unique sink node and enforces this constraint during edge orientation.

components.description: Predictive fidelity evaluation: rationale, protocol, and headline result.

nodes.name: No ground-truth graph exists for direct evaluation
nodes.description: Because the goal is to recover a causal graph over the LLM's latent inference process, there is no ground-truth graph available for direct evaluation.

nodes.name: Predictive fidelity rationale: parents should screen off indirect variables
nodes.description: The learned graphs are evaluated via predictive fidelity: if a graph captures meaningful dependencies, direct causal parents should screen off indirect variables, making them more predictive of a node than other concept subsets.

nodes.name: Post-hoc prediction task compares parent set to all other subsets
nodes.description: For each target node, a multinomial logistic regression is trained to predict it from its graph-based parent set, compared via 10-fold CV to models trained on all other concept subsets that do not fully contain the parent set.

nodes.name: Graph-based predictors outperform average alternative subset in every setting
nodes.description: Graph-based predictors outperform the average alternative subset in every setting, across all models, datasets, and target types, indicating discovered parent sets capture relevant information.

nodes.name: Parent set ranks in Top-3 in most settings
nodes.description: In every setting but one, the causal-graph parent set ranks among the best predictors (Top-3) in a majority of CV cases, despite being compared against tens of alternatives, further strengthening the conclusion.

components.description: Qualitative analysis of learned graphs: convergence vs. divergence across LLMs by task naturalism.

nodes.name: Synthetic Disease Diagnosis concepts consistent across LLMs
nodes.description: On the synthetic Disease Diagnosis dataset, extracted concepts are consistent across LLMs and successfully recover the ground-truth variables (specific symptoms) defining the dataset's generative causal graph.

nodes.name: Even with similar concepts, causal topologies differ
nodes.description: The learned graphs reveal that different LLMs can follow different concept-level reasoning patterns: even when models rely on similar concepts, their causal topologies differ.

nodes.name: Naturalistic tasks show model-specific concept sets, not just topologies
nodes.description: This model-specific structure is even more pronounced in naturalistic Sentiment Analysis and LLM-as-a-Judge tasks, where the extracted concepts themselves vary across models, suggesting models rely on different reasoning mechanisms.

nodes.name: Reasoning differences matter for deployment decisions
nodes.description: These differences matter for deployment: choosing among models requires understanding not only their performance but also whether their underlying reasoning aligns with stakeholders' expectations and constraints.

components.description: MCMC convergence diagnostics: why naive KL decrease is insufficient and the bounded trajectory used instead.

nodes.name: Multi-chain diagnostics inapplicable in single-chain-per-instance setting
nodes.description: Multi-chain diagnostics such as the Gelman-Rubin statistic are not directly applicable because the setting uses a single chain per instance; convergence is instead monitored via the empirical KL divergence over the combinatorial concept-state distribution across iterations.

nodes.name: Naive KL decrease is not sufficient evidence of convergence
nodes.description: A naive KL decrease is not sufficient evidence of convergence, since as the sample pool grows each new counterfactual carries diminishing marginal weight, mechanically reducing KL regardless of genuine stabilization.

nodes.name: Empirical KL bounded between orthogonal-expansion and perfect-overlap extremes
nodes.description: To separate genuine convergence from this artifact, the empirical KL is bounded between an orthogonal-expansion upper bound (every new sample unseen) and a perfect-overlap lower bound (every new sample duplicates an existing one).

nodes.name: Desirable trajectory moves from upper bound toward lower bound
nodes.description: A desirable trajectory begins near the upper bound (actively discovering new valid concept states) and gradually approaches the lower bound (samples increasingly come from a stable, realizable region).

nodes.name: Empirical KL follows the desired trajectory
nodes.description: The empirical KL curve on Sentiment Analysis for GPT-OSS-20B follows precisely this desired trajectory.

nodes.name: Structural stability confirmed once KL stabilizes
nodes.description: Once the KL stabilizes, the Hamming distance between causal edge sets recovered across successive iterations drops to zero, suggesting additional augmentation no longer changes the learned graph.

components.description: Ablation on the contribution of MCMC counterfactual augmentation itself.

nodes.name: Three data regimes compared
nodes.description: The contribution of MCMC expansion is evaluated by comparing three data regimes: All Original, Original Seed (subset seeding the chains), and Seed + Counterfactuals.

nodes.name: Counterfactuals achieve highest predictive accuracy
nodes.description: The counterfactual-augmented regime achieves the highest predictive accuracy for both concept nodes and prediction across all models.

nodes.name: MCMC introduces concept-state combinations absent from original data
nodes.description: The MCMC-generated counterfactuals introduce concept-state combinations absent in the original data, enabling more accurate estimation of dependencies between concepts.

nodes.name: Causal-graph parent subsets outperform average subset (replicated)
nodes.description: Consistent with the predictive fidelity evaluation, the causal graph's parent subsets outperform the average over all concept subsets in this ablation as well.

nodes.name: Together, results demonstrate necessity of the augmentation stage
nodes.description: Together, these two patterns (counterfactual benefit and parent-subset superiority) demonstrate the necessity of the counterfactual augmentation stage.

nodes.name: Contribution 1: causal paradigm for global concept-based explainability
nodes.description: A causal paradigm is introduced for global, concept-based explainability that maps LLM reasoning to causal graphs.

nodes.name: Contribution 2: MCMC-inspired counterfactual augmentation framework
nodes.description: An MCMC-inspired data augmentation framework is proposed that generates counterfactuals to better cover the concept space, enabling robust causal discovery.

nodes.name: Contribution 3: evaluation protocol for structural stability and predictive fidelity
nodes.description: An evaluation protocol is developed for assessing both the structural stability and predictive fidelity of the resulting causal graphs, addressing the absence of gold-standard reasoning graphs.

isolated_nodes.name: Limitation: sensitivity to batch pairing in concept extraction
isolated_nodes.description: Concept extraction runs only once in small batches due to token limits and cost; different batch assignments could highlight distinct contrastive features and yield a different concept set, a limitation future work could mitigate with multiple shuffled extraction passes.

isolated_nodes.name: Limitation: validation restricted to local parents, not full multi-hop chains
isolated_nodes.description: The current validation protocol primarily evaluates local predictive fidelity through discovered parent sets, demonstrating immediate predictors are informative and stable but not directly verifying longer multi-hop causal chains or the broader graph hierarchy.

isolated_nodes.name: Limitation: dependence on self-annotation and generation faithfulness
isolated_nodes.description: The framework relies on the target LLM to annotate concepts, generate counterfactuals, and judge whether edits satisfy constraints; since LLM self-assessments are not guaranteed faithful, errors may propagate despite acceptance criteria mitigating this risk, motivating future external validation or human audits.

isolated_nodes.name: Future work: languages, open-ended generation, multimodal domains
isolated_nodes.description: Future work plans to extend the framework to additional languages, open-ended generation settings, and multimodal domains, broadening evaluation toward standardized, stakeholder-oriented explainability frameworks.
